title: matching of given expression, for -m and -k option, is done in a fuzzy way and produces unexpected results.

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: problem that needs to be addressed

body:
Originally reported by: **Wouter van Ackooy (BitBucket: [w00t0r](http://bitbucket.org/w00t0r), GitHub: [w00t0r](http://github.com/w00t0r))**

---
# Problem
## Functional

The options -m and -k produce strange results. Here are some examples, used with attachment file 'x.py':
- **py.test -k something x.py** --> Matches on the fixture 'something' as well, while it should only match on the function name 'test_something'
- **py.test -k __doc__ x.py** --> Matches both tests, since the keywords contain magic attributes (not only __doc__, but also others like __dict__, __subclasshook__, etc.). Since it is a substring match with the -k option, you can actually do things like 'py.test -k __ x.py' or 'py.test -k sub x.py' to match everything.
- **py.test -m test_something x.py** --> Matches the function name 'test_something', while it should only match on markers. Also happens when providing a classname, like 'TestClass' with the attached file.
- **py.test -m __dict__ x.py** --> Same thing that happens with -k option, described above. It matches on every test, since all of the keywords always contain the magic attributes __dict__, __doc__, etc.
## Technical

The matching functions in _pytest/mark.py, called _matchmark_ and _matchkeyword_, both pass the _eval()_ function a local mapping, based on all of the keywords in the current item.
This means that there is no difference in the way -m and -k match, apart from the fact that -m is a complete string match (BoolDict) and -k is a substring match (SubstringDict).

There is no seperation of the markers and the keywords in the item, since everything is put in the NodeKeywords instance of the item.
# Suggested solutions

There are several things which should be solved in order to make the matching work as expected. So here are some suggestions, which could be adapted. I am not completely sure if some of them will cause any problems with external plugins, so I hope I can get some feedback on them.
## Markers should only match to MarkInfo or MarkDecorator values

In 'matchmark', the NodeKeywords instance from the current item is passed into a BoolDict. This BoolDict will serve as the local mapping for the eval() function. 
So in the __init__ method of the BoolDict class, one could filter the keywords so only MarkInfo and MarkDecorator instances remain. This should solve the issue that markers can also match on magic values or on the name of their parent class for example.

Also, on a side note, I would prefer to refactor the BoolDict and the SubstringDict in addition to this. First of all the naming can be more specific, like MarkerMapping and KeywordMapping, since they are specifically used for providing mappings to markers or keywords. Then instead of passing in a dictionary, maybe just a list of strings can be passed into these mappings. This seems a lot simpler then passing in dictionaries of which then only the keys are used. I am not sure if this could cause any problems with external plugins though.
## Keywords should be seperated, at least for matching functionality.

I'm not sure if NodeKeywords is widely relied upon in external plugins, but it seems like the NodeKeywords instance should not put everyting, from markers to magical attributes and parentnames, in one big dictionary. This makes it hard to filter out the keys that should be matched on, since they are all just string values mapped to a boolean or some wrapper.

So the keywords, the ones to match on with -k, should be put in a seperate internal dictionary of NodeKeywords and possibly accessed from the item directly through a method (so one could call 'colitem.getkeywords()' to get only the keywords to match with the -k option).

For -m, the same can be done, depending if the first suggested solution is favored or this suggestion.

Perhaps any other ideas about the seperation of markers, keywords (the ones to match on) and the rest contained in the NodeKeywords instance of an item?
